title: Generators, yield, and lazy sequences
hook: Generator functions (function*) pause with yield and resume on next() — building lazy sequences without materializing entire datasets. They implement both iterator and iterable in one object.

blocks.text: **function*** defines a generator. Calling it returns a generator object (iterator) without running body until **next()**. **yield** pauses and sends value out; **yield*** delegates to another iterable. Generators are **iterable** — they implement Symbol.iterator returning self. **return()** and **throw()** on iterator interact with yield try/finally inside generator.

entries.plainDefinition: function* returning lazy iterator with yield pauses.
Pauses generator; next() resumes after yield.
Produce values on demand — O(1) memory for infinite streams.
entries.example: function* naturals() { let n=1; while(true) yield n++; }

blocks.text: Paginated API fetch, infinite scroll, and pipeline transforms use generators to avoid loading all rows. Redux-saga and co use generators for async control flow before async/await dominance. C# yield return in IEnumerable is direct analog.

blocks.title: Infinite with guard
blocks.body: Lazy does not mean free — always bound consumer with take(n) or break to avoid infinite loops.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Call generator fn
items.body: Returns generator object — body not executed yet.

items.title: First next()
items.body: Runs until first yield; returns { value, done: false }.

items.title: Subsequent next()
items.body: Resumes after yield until next yield or return.

items.title: Done
items.body: return or end — { done: true, value: undefined }.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Spreading infinite generator. Forgetting generator not run until next(). Not handling throw() into generator. Using generators where simple array map suffices — complexity cost.

blocks.text: Generators compile to **state machines** like async functions. **yield** receives value from next(arg). **Redux-saga** pattern: while(true) { const action = yield take(TYPE) }. Prefer **async/await** for I/O unless need multiple consumers or coroutine style. **Iterator helpers** may replace hand-rolled map filter on iterables.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Thinks generator runs on call like normal function. Cannot explain next() resume. Recommends [...infiniteGen()] without guard.

interviewTakeaways: function* returns generator iterator; body runs lazily on next().
yield pauses; yield* delegates to iterable.
Generators are iterable — for...of and spread work.
Async generators: async function* + for await.
60s: Lazy sequences. C# yield return parallel. Do not spread infinite. Pagination pattern. State machine pause.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "function* runs immediately." Strong: "Returns iterator; next() drives execution to each yield."
Weak: "Generators always better than arrays." Strong: "Use for lazy/infinite; arrays simpler for small finite data."
Strong: "Show paginated fetchPages — yield* items, break early without loading all."
